findings: A huisvestingsvergunning applies to designated regulated rental categories; the permit is linked to both address and occupants.
Current municipal information lists income criteria for private social and regulated mid-market rental housing and requires supporting income, identity and dwelling-rating documents.

priorUseConditions: rented for less than six months at transfer
or already rented under an opkoopbescherming permit/waiver

purchaseProtection.mainRule: Qualifying dwellings may not be given into use during the first four years after registration of the deed of transfer without an applicable permit or waiver.
explicitExclusions: complex sale of at least ten dwellings in one building to one successor owner
new-build housing with a rental prohibition in municipal ground-lease conditions
post-1-April-2022 new-build/transformation designated for rental by ground-lease conditions or agreement
permitGrounds: temporary letting for up to 12 months after owner occupied the dwelling as residence for at least 12 months
dwelling inseparably connected to a shop, office or business premises
partial letting while owner continues to occupy part of the dwelling
waiverGrounds: exceptional circumstances where compliance cannot reasonably be required
socially desirable rental that outweighs the protection objective
simultaneous transfer of four through nine dwellings in one building to one successor owner
applicationEvidence: relevant WOZ value from the calendar year before registration of the deed
temporary rental agreement for the temporary-letting ground
documents proving inseparable connection with business premises where applicable

permitTrigger: 3 or more persons who do not form one household
if owner also lives in the dwelling: rooms rented to 2 or more other persons
statutoryExemptions: occupation by no more than two adults
qualifying inwoning by one additional household
mantelzorg or inwoning of first- through fourth-degree family, subject to regulatory conditions
conditions: communal room at least 11 m2 and at least 3 metres wide
normally one adult per room, or two for married/registered partners
no concurrent holiday-rental or B&B permit
for 4 or more rooms: acoustic requirements under NEN 5077
for 5 or more rooms: fire-safety notification and Bbl compliance
for 7 or more rooms: exceptional-case liveability justification
roomRentalConversion.quotaAndLocation: Quotas apply per neighbourhood and building; availability must be checked for the exact address/building.
roomRentalConversion.omgevingsplanInteraction: An additional environmental/planning permit may be necessary where the applicable omgevingsplan allows only one household.

withdrawal.mainRule: Withdrawing residential space from residential use requires a stock permit unless an explicit exemption applies.
notableExemptions: short stays under six months for designated international-student landing-place housing
qualifying house-sitting arrangements meeting the regulation's conditions
withdrawal.otherUseDecision: A permit for non-residential use may be granted for a socially desired function or a function considered to strengthen the neighbourhood's economic structure.

merger.mainRule: Merging dwellings is part of the stock-permit system.
merger.ownerOccupationException: Municipal guidance states no merger permit is needed where the owner merges an adjacent/above/below dwelling for own occupation and actually lives there.
merger.specialAuthorityException: Some applications in Westpoort and specifically designated areas are handled by Omgevingsdienst Noordzeekanaalgebied.

dwellingFormation.mainRule: A permit is required to convert one dwelling into two or more dwellings.
additionalRules: forming one or more dwellings below 40 m2 is prohibited in districts designated in further rules
required noise and quality standards apply
actual use must be reported within six months
a dwelling formed under a permit applied for after 31 December 2020 cannot be used again as the source dwelling for another formation permit
purchase-protection restrictions can block the permit

splitIntoApartmentRights.workingsgebied: The Amsterdam splitsingsvergunning regime applies to designated pre-1940 buildings in the geographic area in Annex 2, subject to specified exceptions.
splitIntoApartmentRights.mainRule: Within that scope, splitting a building right into apartment rights including residential use is prohibited without a municipal splitsingsvergunning.
splitIntoApartmentRights.quota: The municipality can set area-based quotas for the number of rental dwellings below the liberalisation threshold that may be involved in a split.

citywideRules: all Amsterdam dwellings fall within the tourist-rental scope
holiday rental normally limited to 30 nights per calendar year
each holiday-rental period must be reported in advance
maximum 4 guests at a time according to municipal operational guidance

shortStay.definition: paid use of a dwelling for a period of at most six months, excluding B&B and holiday rental
shortStay.mainRule: Short stay is prohibited without a municipal permit.
shortStay.legacyRule: Older short-stay permits remain subject to the Regional Housing Ordinance Stadsregio Amsterdam 2013 under the transitional provision.

secondHomePiedATerre.mainRule: From 2026 a second home/pied-à-terre in Amsterdam requires a permit.
notableConditionsForExisting2025Cases: permit holder is not registered as resident in Amsterdam
maximum one second home in Amsterdam
used only by the permit holder or members of that household for their own stay
not used as office or holiday rental

temporaryRentalVacancyLaw.mainRule: Temporary rental of a dwelling for sale can be permitted under the Leegstandwet where the municipal conditions are met.
examplesOfConditions: dwelling is for sale and vacant
for private owners, no more than one other temporary-rental permit
one of the specified recent-occupation/new-build/limited-prior-rental conditions must apply

newBuildOwnerOccupancy.mainRule: Amsterdam also uses contractual/policy self-occupancy rental restrictions for qualifying new-build owner-occupied housing; this must remain separate from statutory purchase protection.

findings: Administrative fines can be imposed for violations under the Huisvestingswet according to the ordinance's fine schedule.
After at least two tourist-rental fines in five years, a rental prohibition of up to one year may be imposed.
Existing permits generally continue under the current ordinance, but legacy short-stay permits have a specific transitional regime.
Applications are assessed under the ordinance in force at the time of application.
A hardheidsclausule permits deviation in cases of special hardship, but it is exceptional rather than a standard route.

decisionModelRequirements: Resolve exact BAG address and building before evaluating any Amsterdam rule.
Resolve neighbourhood/district for room-rental quotas, the 15-night tourist-rental override and any area-designated dwelling-formation rules.
Resolve building construction year and Annex-2 location for splitsingsvergunning assessment.
Determine acquisition date, relevant prior rental/use and WOZ value for purchase-protection assessment.
Determine rental/use type: ordinary whole-dwelling rent, room rental, B&B, holiday rental, short stay, second home, temporary letting, merger, withdrawal, dwelling formation or legal split.
Check whether purchase protection independently blocks the requested action.
Check the current omgevingsplan and Omgevingsloket for spatial-use restrictions or an additional omgevingsvergunning.
Check current Nadere regels for quotas, district designations and technical standards before returning a definitive address-level answer.
Keep statutory purchase protection, contractual new-build self-occupancy, Leegstandwet temporary letting and tourist-rental regimes legally separate.
remainingOpenChecks: Machine-readable integration of the current Nadere regels Woonruimteverdeling en Woonruimtevoorraad Amsterdam 2024, especially quota tables and district-specific dwelling-formation rules.
Machine-readable geometry or BAG-to-area mapping for Annex 2 splitsingsvergunning scope and neighbourhood room-rental quotas.
Address-level validation test cases against the current Omgevingsplan Amsterdam.
Product-level legal sign-off remains required before automatically presenting a definitive legal conclusion to end users.
